about: Where two lab instruments may be trusted, from their registered validations. argus_lab.py state prints it, claims --check and argus_ci.py lab validate it, and pyramid plans the fixed-clock screen and the stand-in rung from it. Readings per metric are equivalent, inconclusive, different or not measured; a metric that is not equivalent is a limit on that map.

dm4.note: 13.9 ms was not accepted (lava and routefails read different); 14.25 ms passed a registered confirmation on fresh seeds.

dm2.note: Also accepted at 13.9 ms in the first validation.

dm4.note: Bot kills on the stand-in did not rise with bot skill (Spearman 0.13; skill 3 minus 0 +0.16 a minute, 95 per cent -1.18 to +1.50). Its time in sight of bots ran 0 to 2608 ticks between matches, which swamps the effect. Level at skill 1 matched (1.19 against 1.27) but means nothing without a dose response.

lab_scenarios.about: Generated micro-maps (tools/lab_mapgen.py, the lab_request MCP tool). Each isolates one mechanism and is trusted for isolation-tier claims only.
lab_scenarios.rule: Lab maps are isolation instruments. A result measured on a lab map can support an isolation-tier claim only. A claim about stock geometry needs a separate run on real geometry (dm2, dm3, dm4, dm6 or another stock map), and it cites the lab tapes and the stock tapes together.

lab_voidcorner.intent: Isolate route handoffs at void-edged corners: a 64u walkway ring over lava with four tight 90 degree corners and open air on both sides, so an early waypoint switch or apex corner cut that draws its line across the void shows up as hazard deflections and lava run-offs.
